The 2026-08-28 revision on nysenate.gov added nurse practitioners to the subdivision 7 disability certification, effective 2026-08-25. The only 2026 bill found, S9800 (child restraints in taxis and liveries), is still in Senate committee, so pendingChange is null. IIHS (October 2026) matches the statute.

NC.summary: North Carolina requires children under 8 and under 80 pounds to ride in a weight-appropriate car seat or booster, and children under 5 and under 40 pounds to ride in the back seat when the car has an active front passenger airbag. All passengers under 16 must be buckled up.

rearFacing.text: North Carolina law does not require rear-facing.

harness.text: North Carolina law has no separate harness stage. Children under 8 and under 80 pounds must ride in a weight-appropriate child passenger restraint system.

booster.text: A child under 8 and under 80 pounds must be properly secured in a weight-appropriate child passenger restraint system. The requirement ends when the child turns 8 or reaches 80 pounds.

seatBelt.text: Passengers under 16 must be secured in a child restraint or a seat belt. If no seat with a lap and shoulder belt is available for the car seat, a child under 8 who weighs 40 to 80 pounds may use a properly fitted lap belt alone.

backSeat.text: In a vehicle with an active passenger-side front airbag and a rear seat, a child under 5 and under 40 pounds must ride in the rear seat, unless the child restraint is designed for use with airbags.

penalty.text: A violation carries a fine of up to $25, even if more than one child was unsecured, plus 2 driver license points and no insurance points. A driver charged over a child under 8 can't be convicted if they show the court they have since gotten an approved child restraint for the vehicle the child usually rides in.

NC.exemptions: The law doesn't apply to ambulances or other emergency vehicles, when every seating position with a child restraint or seat belt is occupied, or to vehicles that federal law doesn't require to have seat belts.
NC.agencyName: North Carolina Governor's Highway Safety Program (NCDOT)
NC.notes: The statute's history line ends with S.L. 2007-6. House Bill 368 (2025-2026), 'Revise Child Passenger Restraint Systems Law' (news coverage says it would replace the 80-pound test with a 4'9" height test), passed the House 113-0 on 2025-04-29. A Senate committee substitute was reported on 2026-06-16 and re-referred to Senate Rules, and it has not been enacted, so pendingChange is null; recheck it before publishing. The NCDOT page has no law details beyond 'until they reach age 8 or 80 pounds' and sends readers to the N.C. ND.summary: Children under 8 must ride in a car seat or booster used per the manufacturer's instructions unless they are at least 4'9" tall, in which case a seat belt is enough. Ages 8 through 17 must use a seat belt or a child restraint.

rearFacing.text: No rear-facing requirement in state law.

harness.text: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 8 must be in a child restraint system (car seat or booster) used per the manufacturer's instructions.

booster.text: A child under 8 must be in a child restraint system (car seat or booster). A child under 8 who is at least 57 inches (4'9") tall is not required to use one but must be correctly buckled in a safety belt.

seatBelt.text: Children 8 through 17 must be in an approved child restraint or correctly buckled in a safety belt. A child under 8 who is at least 4'9" may use a seat belt.

backSeat.text: No back-seat requirement in law. The state health department recommends children under 13 ride in the back.

penalty.text: $25 fee (N.D.C.C. § 39-06.1-06) and 1 point against the driver's license (§ 39-06.1-10). The driver is responsible.

ND.exemptions: Does not apply in vehicles that were not equipped with safety belts when manufactured, or when a child is transported in an emergency.
ND.agencyName: North Dakota Health and Human Services
ND.notes: The legislature's chapter PDF has no amendment history line, so the date of the last amendment to 39-21-41.2 is not confirmed (left null). Secondary enforcement (39-21-41.5) was repealed by S.L. 2023, ch. 362.

OH.summary: Children under 4 or under 40 pounds must ride in a car seat, and children under 8 who are shorter than 4'9" must ride in a booster. Children 8 through 15 must use a car seat or a seat belt.

rearFacing.text: No rear-facing requirement in state law.

harness.text: A child who is under 4 years old or weighs under 40 pounds must be secured in a child restraint system that meets federal standards, per the manufacturer's instructions.

booster.text: A child under 8 and under 4'9" who no longer needs a car seat must be secured on a booster seat that meets federal standards.

seatBelt.text: Children 8 through 15 must be restrained in a child restraint system or a seat belt. Police may not stop a driver solely for a booster (age 4-7) or age 8-15 belt violation; those rules are secondary enforcement.

backSeat.text: No back-seat requirement in law.

penalty.text: First offense is a minor misdemeanor with a fine of $25 to $75; a repeat offense is a fourth-degree misdemeanor. Several unrestrained children at the same time and place count as one violation. Fines go to the child highway safety fund.

OH.exemptions: Taxicabs and public safety vehicles; emergencies that threaten life; a child with a physical impairment documented by an affidavit from a physician, clinical nurse specialist, certified nurse practitioner or chiropractor (the child must be restrained as the affidavit recommends). Child care center and nursery school vehicles follow their own rule.
OH.notes: Verified from the statute (current version effective 2025-03-20, S.B. 196). Ohio Department of Health car seat pages (Ohio Buckles Buckeyes) did not render for automated reading, so no agency or inspection URL is given. No 2025-26 bill adding a rear-facing rule was found.

OK.summary: Children under 2 ride rear-facing (or until they outgrow the rear-facing seat) and children under 4 ride in a car seat. Children 4 to 7 who are not taller than 4'9" must use a car seat or booster; at 8, or once taller than 4'9", a seat belt is enough.

rearFacing.text: The child restraint must be rear-facing until the child turns 2 or reaches the rear-facing seat's height or weight limit, whichever comes first.

harness.text: A child under 4 must be properly secured in a child passenger restraint system.

booster.text: A child at least 4 but younger than 8, if not taller than 4'9", must be secured in a child passenger restraint system or booster seat.

seatBelt.text: If a child is 8 or taller than 4'9", a properly secured seat belt meets the law. The general belt law (47 O.S. § 12-417) covers drivers and front-seat passengers.

backSeat.text: No back-seat requirement in law.

penalty.text: $50 fine plus court costs. For a first offense the fine is suspended and court costs are capped at $15 with proof of buying or borrowing a child restraint. The Department of Public Safety may not assess points.

OK.exemptions: School buses, taxicabs, mopeds, motorcycles and vehicles not required to have belts; ambulances and emergency vehicles; vehicles with all belts in use; children with a physician's written medical exemption; a child over 40 pounds in a back seat with only lap belts (or when the lap-shoulder belts are used by other children over 40 pounds); and forward-facing use for a child under 4 by a driver with a disability placard or plate and a DPS forward-facing exemption letter.
OK.agencyName: Oklahoma State Department of Health, Injury Prevention Service
OK.notes: Free seat checks are by appointment at county health departments (OSDH page), so fitStationUrl is the county health department map. SB 464 (2025-26), which would have rewritten the restraint rules, was referred to Senate Public Safety in Feb. 2025 and never advanced. IIHS footnote: the statute says '8 years of age', not '8 or older'.

OR.summary: Children under 2 must ride rear-facing and children 40 pounds or less must ride in a car seat. Children over 40 pounds must use a booster until they are taller than 4'9" or turn 8.

rearFacing.text: A person under 2 years of age must be secured with a child safety system in a rear-facing position.

harness.text: A child who weighs 40 pounds or less must be secured in a child safety system designed for children 40 pounds or less.

booster.text: A child over 40 pounds who is 4'9" or shorter must use a child safety system that raises the child so the belt fits (a booster). From age 8 a child may use a seat belt instead.

seatBelt.text: A person taller than 4'9", or any child 8 or older, must be secured with a safety belt or harness. The driver is responsible for passengers under 16.

backSeat.text: No back-seat requirement in law (ODOT). A rear-facing seat cannot go in front of an active airbag.

penalty.text: Class D traffic violation: presumptive fine $115, maximum $250 (ORS 153.019, 153.018).

OR.exemptions: Booster rule does not apply in a rear seat with only lap belts (if the child uses the lap belt) or if the child uses a harness seat rated over 40 pounds. ORS 811.215 lists other exemptions, including for-hire vehicles' child seat duty, vehicles not required to have belts, a DMV medical exemption certificate (ORS 811.220), and when all seating positions are occupied.
OR.notes: Statute text is the 2025 edition. The 2026 amended/repealed table shows no changes to ORS 811.210, 811.215 or 153.019. Last amendment to 811.210 was 2017 c.177 (ODOT notes the rear-facing-to-2 rule applies to children who turned 1 on or after May 26, 2017).

PA.summary: Children under 2 must ride rear-facing and children under 4 must ride in a car seat. Children 4 to 7 must ride in a booster, and children 8 to 17 must wear a seat belt.

rearFacing.text: A child under 2 must be fastened in a rear-facing child passenger restraint system, used until the child outgrows the manufacturer's maximum weight and height limits.

harness.text: A child under 4 must be fastened in a child passenger restraint system anywhere in the vehicle, including the cargo area.

booster.text: A child 4 or older but under 8 must be fastened in a seat belt and an appropriately fitting booster seat. There is no height exemption.

seatBelt.text: The driver must secure every occupant 8 or older but under 18 in a properly adjusted seat belt.

backSeat.text: No back-seat requirement in law. PennDOT recommends the back seat through age 12.

penalty.text: Summary offense with a $75 fine for car seat or booster violations; the 8-17 belt rule carries a $10 fine. Not a moving violation. Charges are dismissed if the driver shows the judge proof of acquiring a child seat or booster before or at the hearing. Insurers may not raise premiums for a conviction.

PA.exemptions: PennDOT may grant exemptions when a car seat or booster is impractical for physical reasons, including medical reasons or the child's size.
PA.notes: Child seat stages were last changed by Act 43 of 2016; the section was last amended by Act 61 of 2024 (adult belt rule). PennDOT points readers to the PennDOT-funded TIPP fitting station directory (https://pakidstravelsafe.org/resources/car-seat-check-fitting-station-locations/), which is not a state-run page, so fitStationUrl is left null.

RI.summary: Children under 2 or under 30 pounds must ride rear-facing, and children under 8 who are under 57 inches and under 80 pounds must ride in a car seat or booster in a rear seat. All children under 8 ride in a rear seat, and children 8 to 17 must wear a seat belt.

rearFacing.text: All infants and toddlers under 2 or weighing less than 30 pounds must be restrained in a rear-facing car seat.

harness.text: Not required as a separate stage. The law says children 2 and older, or who have outgrown the rear-facing seat, should use a forward-facing harnessed seat up to the manufacturer's maximum.

booster.text: A child under 8, under 57 inches and under 80 pounds must ride in a federally approved child restraint system in a rear seating position.

seatBelt.text: A child under 8 who is at least 57 inches or at least 80 pounds must wear a seat belt in a rear seat. Children 8 to 17 must wear a seat belt in any seat.

backSeat.text: Children under 8 must ride in a rear seating position. They may ride in front, properly restrained, only if the vehicle has no back seat or all rear seats are used by other children.

penalty.text: $100 under the state violation schedule (§ 31-41.1-4) for no child restraint or for a child not in a rear seat; $40 for a passenger 8-17 without a belt. A child restraint citation is voided if proof of buying an approved seat is shown to the issuing police department within 7 days. Violations are not recorded on the driving record.

RI.exemptions: Front-seat placement is allowed if there is no back seat or all rear positions are used by other children. The 8-17 belt rule does not apply to pre-July 1966 vehicles, vehicles not required to have belts, a person with a physician's written verification (up to 12 months), or postal letter carriers on duty.
RI.notes: Verified from the statute and the statutory fine schedule. RI DMV and State Police car seat pages blocked automated access (HTTP 403) and were not read, so no agency URL is given. A search snippet of the DMV page cites an $85 fine, which conflicts with the current statutory schedule ($100); IIHS also lists $100.

SC.summary: Children under 2 ride rear-facing and then in a harnessed forward-facing seat until they outgrow it; children 4 and up who have outgrown the harness use a booster until age 8 or 57 inches and a proper belt fit. Children under 8 must ride in the back seat.

rearFacing.text: A child under 2 must ride in a rear-facing seat in a rear seat until the child exceeds the seat's height or weight limit.

harness.text: A child 2 or older (or under 2 who has outgrown rear-facing) must ride in a forward-facing harnessed seat in a rear seat until exceeding the seat's highest height or weight limit. Only a child at least 4 who has outgrown it may move to a booster.

booster.text: A child at least 4 who has outgrown the forward-facing seat must use a belt-positioning booster with a lap and shoulder belt in a rear seat until meeting the adult-belt height and fit requirements.

seatBelt.text: A child at least 8 or at least 57 inches tall may use an adult belt if it fits: lap belt across the thighs and hips, shoulder belt across the center of the chest, and knees bent at the seat edge without slouching. Drivers must make occupants 17 and under wear a belt or ride in a child restraint.

backSeat.text: Children under 8 must ride in a rear seat. They may ride in front, in the proper seat, only if there is no rear seat or all rear seats are occupied by children under 8.

penalty.text: Fine of not more than $150. The court must waive the fine if, before or on the court date, the driver shows proof of acquiring, buying or renting an appropriate child restraint.

SC.exemptions: Taxi drivers; emergency vehicles in an emergency; church, day care and school bus drivers; public transportation; commercial vehicles. A child with a documented medical need (physician, advanced nurse practitioner or physician assistant) may use a restraint designed for that need.
SC.agencyName: South Carolina Department of Public Safety
SC.notes: The SCDPS law web page (node/2243) returned 404, so agencyUrl points to SCDPS's CPS guide PDF, which matches the statute.

SD.summary: Children under 5 must ride in a child restraint system, unless they weigh at least 40 pounds, in which case a seat belt is enough. Passengers 5 to 17 must wear a seat belt.

rearFacing.text: No rear-facing requirement in state law.

harness.text: A child under 5 must be secured in a child passenger restraint system per the manufacturer's instructions. A child under 5 who weighs at least 40 pounds may use a seat belt instead.

booster.text: No booster seat requirement in state law.

seatBelt.text: The driver must make sure passengers at least 5 and under 18 wear a properly adjusted seat belt. Drivers and passengers 14 to 17 must also wear one themselves.

backSeat.text: No back-seat requirement in law.

penalty.text: A violation is a petty offense (handled as a civil proceeding). The statute does not set the fine amount.

SD.exemptions: Does not apply in passenger cars made before 1966 that were not equipped with seat belts.
SD.notes: Verified from the statute (SL 1998, ch. 199 is the latest source note). No state agency car seat page was found. The fine amount for a petty offense is not in the statute; IIHS lists a $25 maximum base fine, but it was not confirmed from an official South Dakota source. 2025 SB 165 (Larson) proposed changes; the codified law is unchanged, so it was not enacted.

TN.summary: Children under 1 or 20 pounds or less ride rear-facing; ages 1 through 3 over 20 pounds ride in a harnessed car seat; ages 4 through 8 under 4'9" ride in a booster, all in the rear seat if available. Children 9 through 12, or any child 12 or younger who is 4'9" or taller, must use a seat belt.

rearFacing.text: Children under 1, or any child weighing 20 pounds or less, must ride in a rear-facing child restraint in the rear seat if available.

harness.text: Children 1 through 3 weighing more than 20 pounds must ride in a harnessed child safety seat (rear- or forward-facing) in the rear seat if available.

booster.text: Children 4 through 8 who are shorter than 4'9" must ride in a belt-positioning booster in the rear seat if available.

seatBelt.text: Children 9 through 12, or any child 12 or younger who is 4'9" or taller, must use a seat belt; the rear seat is recommended. Children 13 through 15 must use a seat belt.

backSeat.text: Children in rear-facing, harnessed or booster seats (through age 8) must ride in the rear seat if available. The rear seat is recommended, not required, for ages 9 through 12.

penalty.text: Each unrestrained child 8 or younger is a separate violation, with court costs; the statute makes it a Class C misdemeanor, and a court may order a first offender to attend a child passenger safety class. For the age 9-12 belt rule, only one citation per vehicle is issued: a $50 fine with no court costs or litigation taxes.

TN.exemptions: A child who cannot safely use a standard restraint may use a specially modified one if the driver carries a physician's signed prescription.
TN.notes: The official Tennessee Code is hosted by LexisNexis and could not be read automatically, so statuteUrl is null. Stage rules come from the THSO law card and the 2025 Department of Safety release (which names tntrafficsafety.org/cps as the inspection-site finder; that page itself returned 403). Penalty details come from UT MTAS (reviewed 07/2026) and an unofficial FindLaw copy (Class C misdemeanor). MTAS says 9-12 year olds under 4'9" must be in a booster; the THSO card, FindLaw text and IIHS all say 9-12 use a seat belt, which is what we used. The Class C fine amount was not confirmed from an official page, so fineFirst is null.

TX.summary: Children younger than 8 must ride in a child safety seat or booster, used per the manufacturer's instructions, unless they are taller than 4'9". Children 8 to 16 must wear a seat belt.

rearFacing.text: No rear-facing requirement in state law.

harness.text: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 8 must be in a child passenger safety seat system per the manufacturer's instructions.

booster.text: A child younger than 8 must be secured in a child passenger safety seat system (car seat or booster) unless the child is taller than 4'9".

seatBelt.text: A child younger than 17 who is not required to be in a child seat must be secured by a seat belt in any belted seat. Passengers 15 and older are personally responsible for buckling up.

backSeat.text: No back-seat requirement in law.

penalty.text: Misdemeanor with a fine of $25 to $250. It is a defense if the driver had no child seat in the vehicle, was not cited for anything else, was not in a crash, and later obtains an appropriate seat.

TX.exemptions: Defense if driving in an emergency or for a law enforcement purpose. Does not apply to vehicles transporting passengers for hire (except contracted non-emergency Medicaid transport), or when all seating positions with belts or child seats are occupied.
TX.notes: Fine range is $25-$250 per the current statute (the old $25 first-offense rule was repealed in 2011); TxDOT also says fines can reach $250. Last change to 545.412 took effect June 1, 2023 (repeal of subsection (g)); 545.4121 was amended effective Sept. 1, 2023.

UT.summary: Children younger than 8 must ride in a child restraint device used per the manufacturer's instructions, unless they are 57 inches or taller. Children 8 to 15 must wear a seat belt.

rearFacing.text: No rear-facing requirement in state law.

harness.text: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 8 must be in a child restraint device used per the manufacturer's instructions.

booster.text: Each person younger than 8 must be in a child restraint device (car seat or booster). A child under 8 who is 57 inches or taller is exempt and must wear a seat belt.

seatBelt.text: The driver must secure each child 8 and older (and under 16) in a properly adjusted seat belt. Passengers 16 and older must buckle up themselves.

backSeat.text: No back-seat requirement in law.

penalty.text: Infraction with a maximum fine of $45. The court must waive the whole fine for a first child-restraint violation with proof of acquiring, renting or buying a child restraint. No points. Several unrestrained occupants count as one offense.

UT.exemptions: Vehicles made before July 1, 1966 or not required to have belts; a person with a physician or physician assistant's written verification; a passenger when all seats are occupied; public transit vehicles over 10,000 pounds. In a taxi or rideshare, the supervising adult passenger is responsible for the child's restraint.
UT.notes: The statute's belt clause reads 'at least eight years old and no less than 16 years old', an apparent drafting error for 'younger than 16'. H.B. 574 (2026) would have added rear-facing, harness and booster stages and a back seat rule for under-13s; it was not enacted (the code still shows only the 2024 version of 41-6a-1803 and the 2018 version of 41-6a-1805). The Highway Safety Office's own car seat page returned 404; its FAQ confirms the $45 citation and that Utah law does not say where a child must sit.

VT.summary: Children under 2 must ride rear-facing with a harness, children under 5 in a harnessed seat (rear- or forward-facing), and children under 8 in a booster if not in a harnessed seat. Children under 18 must otherwise wear a seat belt, and children under 13 ride in the back seat when practical.

rearFacing.text: A child under 2 must be secured in a federally approved rear-facing child restraint with a harness.

harness.text: A child under 5 not in a rear-facing seat must be in a forward-facing harnessed seat until reaching the seat's weight or height limit.

booster.text: A child under 8 who is not in a harnessed car seat must be secured in a booster seat. There is no height exemption.

seatBelt.text: A child under 18 who is not in a harnessed seat or booster must be restrained in a seat belt.

backSeat.text: A child under 13 must always, if practical, ride in a rear seat. A rear-facing seat may not be placed in front of an active passenger airbag.

penalty.text: Civil penalty of $25 for a first violation, $50 for a second, and $100 for a third or later violation.

VT.exemptions: Type I school buses; vehicles regularly used to carry passengers for hire (except child care facility vehicles); vehicles manufactured without belts; and evacuations ordered by an enforcement officer, firefighter or civil authority.
VT.agencyName: Vermont Department of Health (Be Seat Smart)
VT.notes: Current rules took effect July 1, 2024 (2023 Acts 85 and 165, Adj. Sess.). IIHS describes the harness stage as '3 through 4'; the statute covers every child under 5 who is not rear-facing.

VA.summary: Children up to age 8 must ride in a child safety seat, rear-facing until at least age 2 (or until reaching the seat maker's minimum forward-facing weight), in the back seat. Passengers under 18 must otherwise wear a seat belt.

rearFacing.text: A child restraint may not face forward until the child reaches 2 years of age or the minimum weight for a forward-facing seat set by its manufacturer.

harness.text: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 8 must be in a child restraint device that meets federal standards, chosen per the manufacturer's instructions.

booster.text: Any child up to age 8 (through age 7) must be secured in a federally approved child restraint device (car seat or booster). There is no height exemption.

seatBelt.text: Anyone transporting a person under 18 who is not required to be in a child restraint must make sure that person is properly secured by a seat belt.

backSeat.text: Child restraint devices must be placed in the back seat. If the vehicle has no back seat, the seat may go in the front passenger seat only if there is no passenger airbag or it has been deactivated.

penalty.text: $50 civil penalty, not suspendable, for a first violation; up to $500 for a second or later violation on a different date. No demerit points and no court costs. The court may waive the penalty if the driver could not afford a child seat. Fines go to the Child Restraint Device Special Fund.

VA.exemptions: Taxicabs, school buses, executive sedans and limousines. A child exempted by a physician (weight, height, physical unfitness or medical reason) must carry the signed statement; failing to carry it is a $20 penalty. Emergency and law enforcement vehicles under exigent circumstances when no seat is available.
VA.notes: Back-seat rule: the statute says all child restraint devices go in the back seat. IIHS and the VDH page say only rear-facing devices must; we followed the statute.

WA.summary: Children under 2 ride rear-facing and children under 4 ride in a harnessed seat until they outgrow it; after that, children ride in a booster until they are 4'9" tall. Children under 13 ride in the back seat where practical.

rearFacing.text: A child under 2 must be in a rear-facing child restraint until reaching the seat's weight or height limit.

harness.text: A child under 4 who is not rear-facing must be in a forward-facing harnessed seat until reaching the seat's weight or height limit.

booster.text: A child who is not in a rear-facing or harnessed seat and is under 4'9" must be in a booster seat (there is no age cutoff). The booster rule does not apply where only a lap belt is available.

seatBelt.text: A child under 16 who has outgrown the booster stage must be secured with a properly adjusted and fastened seat belt.

backSeat.text: A driver transporting a child under 13 must use the back seat where it is practical to do so.

penalty.text: Traffic infraction. Child restraint violations are not listed in the court penalty schedule, so the default base penalty of $48 plus statutory assessments applies (local court rules may differ). The ticket is dismissed if the driver shows proof of getting an approved child seat or booster within 7 days and has never had one dismissed before.

WA.exemptions: For-hire vehicles; auto transportation company vehicles for 16 or fewer passengers; parking, hotel, convention and airport shuttles; school buses. The booster rule does not apply in seats with only a lap belt.
WA.notes: Verified from the statute and court rule IRLJ 6.2(b). The WTSC child passenger safety URL now redirects to a mini-grants page and the DCYF page returned 404, so no agency URL is given. IIHS lists the maximum base fine as $250; the statute itself sets no amount.

WV.summary: Children under 8 must ride in a child passenger safety seat (car seat or booster) unless they are at least 4'9" tall, in which case a seat belt is enough. Passengers under 18 in the back seat and everyone in front must wear a belt.

rearFacing.text: No rear-facing requirement in state law.

harness.text: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 8 must be in a federally approved child passenger safety device.

booster.text: A child under 8 must be in a federally approved child passenger safety device system (which includes a booster). If the child is under 8 and at least 4'9" tall, a seat belt meets the law.

seatBelt.text: The driver, every front-seat passenger, and back-seat passengers under 18 must wear a seat belt (W. Va. Code § 17C-15-49, $25 fine, no points).

backSeat.text: No back-seat requirement in law.

penalty.text: Misdemeanor with a fine of $10 to $20.

WV.exemptions: Vehicles operated for hire. A driver is not in violation if every seat belt is in use and there are more passengers than belts.
WV.agencyName: West Virginia Governor's Highway Safety Program
WV.notes: Last amended by 2005 S.B. 414. GHSP describes it as a primary enforcement law.

WI.summary: Children under 1 or under 20 pounds ride rear-facing, and children under 4 or under 40 pounds ride in a rear- or forward-facing car seat, in the back seat if there is one. Children 4 to 7 who weigh 40 to 80 pounds and are 4'9" or shorter ride in a car seat or booster.

rearFacing.text: A child less than 1 year old, or less than 20 pounds, must be in a rear-facing child seat in the back seat (if the vehicle has one).

harness.text: A child at least 1 and 20 pounds but under 4 or under 40 pounds must be in a forward- or rear-facing child seat in the back seat (if the vehicle has one).

booster.text: A child from age 4 to 8 who weighs 40 to 80 pounds and is no more than 4'9" must be in a child seat or a booster seat.

seatBelt.text: All drivers and passengers over age 4 must wear seat belts; drivers are responsible for unbelted passengers 4 to 16.

backSeat.text: Children who must ride in a rear- or forward-facing car seat (under 4 or under 40 pounds) must be in the back seat if the vehicle has one. The booster stage has no back-seat rule.

penalty.text: WisDOT lists the total penalty as $175.30 if the child is under 4, and $150.10 for a first offense, $200.50 for a second and $263.50 for a third or later offense if the child is 4 to 8. The base forfeiture is $30-$75 (under 4) or $10-$25 (ages 4-8).

WI.exemptions: WisDOT says no exemption allows taking a child out of the restraint for personal needs such as feeding or diapering. Statutory exemptions were not confirmed.
WI.notes: docs.legis.wisconsin.gov did not resolve (DNS failure) during research, so the statute text was not read. All rules are from WisDOT pages, which is why exemptions and the last amendment date are unconfirmed. statuteUrl is the link WisDOT gives. WisDOT's 'where to have seats checked' link goes to Safe Kids Wisconsin (not a state page), so fitStationUrl is null.

WY.summary: Children under 9 must ride in a child safety restraint, in a seat other than the front seat when possible, unless the vehicle's lap and shoulder belt fits them properly. Every passenger must wear a seat belt, and drivers must buckle up passengers under 12.

rearFacing.text: No rear-facing requirement in state law. A rear-facing infant seat may not be placed in front of an active airbag.

harness.text: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 9 must be in a child safety restraint system used per the manufacturer's instructions.

booster.text: Each child who has not reached their ninth birthday must be secured in a child safety restraint system (car seat or booster). The exception: a child whose lap and shoulder belt fits properly across the collarbone, chest and hips.

seatBelt.text: Every driver and passenger must wear a seat belt, and the driver must make sure passengers under 12 wear one. A child under 9 may use the belt alone only if it fits properly.

backSeat.text: Children under 9 must ride in a seat other than the front seat. They may ride in front if the vehicle has only one row of seats or all rear belts are used by other child passengers.

penalty.text: Fine of up to $50 for a first offense, waived if the driver shows the court they bought, leased or got a proper restraint after the offense. Up to $100 for a second or later offense. Using a restraint against the manufacturer's instructions is also a violation.

WY.exemptions: A child with a physician's signed statement (carried in the vehicle) that the child's weight or condition requires not using a restraint; a driver giving aid to the child or parent; a child whose lap and shoulder belt fits properly. The law does not cover emergency and law enforcement vehicles, school buses (including private school or church buses used for school or church trips), or public transportation buses built without belts.
WY.notes: Verified from the statute (Title 31 PDF compiled May 2026). No WYDOT car seat page was found (the old occupant protection URL returns 404). HB0026 (2025), which would have required rear-facing seats to age 2, was not considered for introduction. IIHS lists 'adult belt permissible: not permissible' for children 8 and under, but the statute allows a properly fitting lap and shoulder belt.
